references.text: Abraham buys the cave of Machpelah as a burial place from Ephron the Hittite. It is in this cave that Jacob's sons bury him, just as he had asked.
Jacob gives his sons instructions to bury him in the cave of Machpelah, which is fulfilled in Genesis 50:13.
Isaac and Ishmael bury their father Abraham in the cave of Machpelah, the same family burial place where Jacob is later buried by his sons.
Joseph's bones are buried in Shechem, not in the cave of Machpelah—unlike Jacob, who was buried in Machpelah.
Prophetic fulfillment: Jacob's wish to be buried in the cave of Machpelah (49:30) is realized through the actual burial of Joseph (50:13).
Theological parallel: Confirmation that both Abraham (25:9) and Jacob (50:13) were buried in the same holy purchased burial site, symbolizing God's promise of the land.
Historical context: The origin of the burial place (Sarah's burial in 23:19) explains why it was the chosen location for Jacob's burial in 50:13.

Confirmation of ownership rights: The status of the field as Abraham's purchased inheritance (25:10) underscores its significance as the final resting place for the entire patriarchal family in 50:13.
Legal basis: The formal transfer of the property (23:20) is the necessary condition that allowed the patriarchs to be buried there in 50:13.
Detailed context: The description of the complete transfer (23:17) reinforces the importance of the entire property being used as the burial place for the patriarchs in 50:13.
